records.question: Week 5 report with totals grouped by project type

report.title: Week 5 Report with Totals Grouped by Project Type
report.sql:
SELECT pt.name AS project_type, COUNT(ptask.id) AS ticket_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ptask.task_status = 'Completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_tasks, COUNT(ptask.id) - SUM(CASE WHEN ptask.task_status = 'Completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_tasks, ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN ptask.task_status = 'Completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0) / NULLIF(COUNT(ptask.id), 0), 2) AS progress FROM projects p JOIN project_type pt ON p.project_type_id = pt.id LEFT JOIN product_task ptask ON p.id = ptask.project_id AND ptask.is_deleted = 0 GROUP BY pt.id, pt.name ORDER BY pt.name
LIMIT 500
report.explanation: This query retrieves ticket counts and progress metrics grouped by project type for a Week 5 style report. It joins projects with project_type to categorize by type, then left joins product_task to count total tickets and completed tasks. The progress percentage is calculated as completed tasks divided by total tickets. The query filters out deleted tasks and groups results by project type name.
assumptions: Project type is determined by the project_type_id foreign key in the projects table linking to project_type
Task completion is identified by task_status = 'Completed' in the product_task table
Deleted tasks (is_deleted = 1) should be excluded from counts
The report should include all projects regardless of their current status

New tickets are defined as product_task records created within the year 2026

records.question: Find projects with zero completed tasks but more than 5 total tasks

report.title: Projects with Zero Completed Tasks but More Than 5 Total Tasks
report.sql:
SELECT p.id AS project_id, p.project_name, COUNT(pt.id) AS total_tasks, SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(pt.task_status) IN ('completed', 'done', 'closed') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_tasks FROM projects p LEFT JOIN product_task pt ON p.id = pt.project_id AND pt.is_deleted = 0 GROUP BY p.id, p.project_name HAVING completed_tasks = 0 AND total_tasks > 5
LIMIT 500
report.explanation: This query joins the projects table with product_task to count total tasks and completed tasks per project. It filters for non-deleted tasks and uses a case-insensitive check for common completion status values. The HAVING clause returns only projects where completed_tasks equals 0 and total_tasks exceeds 5.
assumptions: Task completion is indicated by task_status values containing 'completed', 'done', or 'closed' (case-insensitive)
Only non-deleted tasks (is_deleted = 0) should be counted
Each row in product_task represents a distinct task for counting purposes

records.question: Show projects where completion percentage is below 50 percent

report.title: Projects with Completion Percentage Below 50%
report.sql:
SELECT p.project_name, COUNT(pt.id) AS total_tasks, SUM(CASE WHEN pt.task_status IN ('Completed', 'Done', 'Finished', 'complete') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_tasks, ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN pt.task_status IN ('Completed', 'Done', 'Finished', 'complete') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(pt.id)), 2) AS completion_percentage FROM projects p LEFT JOIN product_task pt ON p.id = pt.project_id AND pt.is_deleted = 0 GROUP BY p.id, p.project_name HAVING completion_percentage < 50 AND total_tasks > 0
LIMIT 500
report.explanation: This query calculates the completion percentage for each project by counting total non-deleted tasks and completed tasks (where task_status indicates completion). It then filters to show only projects where the completion percentage is below 50% and have at least one task.
assumptions: Task completion is determined by task_status values: 'Completed', 'Done', 'Finished', or 'complete'
Only non-deleted tasks (is_deleted = 0) are counted
Projects with no tasks are excluded from results
Completion percentage is calculated as (completed_tasks / total_tasks) * 100
